messages:
Maria (eng-platform): Heads-up — product wants a single dashboard showing request-level correlation for user-facing routes. Need runtime and infra inputs on headers, sampling, and cardinality.

Tao (eng-runtime): We can emit x-request-id + span_id. Runtime already generates trace_id/span_id in headers for internal calls. For external requests we set x-request-id if absent.

Sam (eng-infra): Question: what's the retention and cardinality? If we index full request-id we'll blow up the metrics store. Prefer rollup counters + sampled trace indexing.

Jess (product): For rollout UX we need per-route p95 latency, error rate, and a "trace link" count for sampled traces. Not every request needs a trace — product wants an easy way to see sampled traces for a row.

Tao (eng-runtime): Proposed sampling: deterministic sampling key = hash(user_id || route) with rate 1% by default, adjustable per-route. Also emit an 'is_sampled' boolean tag on metrics so dashboards can roll up both sampled and unsampled counts.

Anya (eng-sre): Ops concern: we need a force-sample mechanism for canaries and incident investigations. Suggest header X-Force-Trace: 1 but only accepted from internal IP ranges / authenticated services.

Kai (eng-ml): For model-backed routes show model_version and quantization profile in trace tags. We'll need runtime to attach model_version before sending spans.

DevexBot: deploy-bot: New config pushed to runtime: tracing.sample.default=0.01 (see infra deploy 2026-03-18T09:12Z).

Maria (eng-platform): UX ask — dashboard row should include: route, customer_tier, model_version, p50/p95 latency, error rate, sampled_trace_rate, and a trace link. Link pattern: /traces?trace_id={{trace_id}}. If no trace available, show disabled link.

Sam (eng-infra): Implementation notes: We will emit two metric families: request.count (tags: route, model_version, customer_tier, sampled=true/false) and request.sampled_spans (count of sampled spans). We will NOT index raw request IDs in metrics; instead keep a short-lived trace index (TTL 7d) for trace lookups to avoid high-cardinality bill.

Tao (eng-runtime): Example header propagation + sampling config (runtime will accept these and attach tags):

```
# headers
X-Request-Id: uuid-v4
X-Trace-Id: 1af7651916cd43dd8448eb211c80319c
X-Span-Id: 00f067aa0ba902b7
X-Force-Trace: 1  # only from internal ranges

# sampling config (pseudo)
sampling: {
  default: 0.01,
  per_route: {"/api/generate": 0.02, "/api/health": 0.0},
  key: "hash(user_id||route)"
}
```

Maria (eng-platform): Agreed. Next steps: eng-runtime to post the sample event schema + example span payload; eng-infra to propose dashboard rollup queries and retention; devex/product to draft UX copy and the row mock by EOD Friday. @Sam @Tao please confirm owners.

Anya (eng-sre): I'll own the canary force-sample gating and audit. +1 on 7d TTL for initial indexing.

Jess (product): I'll mock the dashboard rows and the trace link behavior — will post a screenshot in this thread by Thursday.

Tao (eng-runtime): I'll post the sample schema and an example event here tomorrow morning.

Sam (eng-infra): I'll put together the ES rollup query + Grafana rollup panel and post a draft by Friday.

Maria (eng-platform): Thanks everyone — this is the cross-team plan. We'll sync briefly in standup tomorrow for blockers. :thumbsup:
